The invasion and related events are creating additional upward pressure on inflation and are likely to weigh on economic activity—consistent with an adverse supply (cost-push) shock in New Keynesian models (e.g., Galí), where energy price spikes and supply-chain disruptions raise prices while depressing output. Evidence on energy price shocks shows negative growth effects (VAR-based findings) and higher rates can transmit via cost and credit channels (Curdia and Woodford, 2008), amplifying near-term headwinds. The FOMC’s rate hikes and balance-sheet reduction are in line with inflation-forecast–targeting and Taylor-rule style frameworks (Svensson and Woodford, 2005; Romer and Romer), aiming to anchor expectations and limit medium-term sacrifice ratios despite near-term weakness. Overall tone: slightly negative with elevated inflation risk but supported by a credible policy response.
